transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm in the right place, and I really don't want to waste your time. But, well, I've been having a bit of trouble at home lately. 

It sounds kind of silly, to be honest, and I'm a little embarrassed to even admit it, but... I spend most of my day just going back over the same things. Like the electrical outlets, the locks on the doors, my tools, and even just dust around the house. I just keep checking them and fixing them, again and again. I end up doing it until I'm completely worn out, but I still just don't feel sure enough to leave it alone. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay for you.
Can you tell me what goes through your mind when you're checking the outlets, locks, or cleaning? Are these thoughts something you don't want, but feel like you have to follow through with?

Yes, exactly. You understand it perfectly, doctor. It's just... well, I really don't want you to think badly of me, or think I'm crazy, but... yeah, they aren't thoughts I want at all. 

Even when I know for a fact I did a job right around the house, these... just really ugly thoughts keep jumping into my head. I'll start worrying that maybe a loose wire I missed is going to spark and burn the whole house down, or... or that a nail I left somewhere on the floor is going to hurt my wife. 

I really try to just push them out of my head, because I know I'm probably overreacting, but... they just come right back, and usually they come back stronger until I finally give in and go check. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answer, I just want to make sure I'm explaining it the way you need.
